scope: QualityBlock1990s generated danchi facade and balcony weathering

benchmarkContext.regionModel: Kanto-class Japanese new-town climate context; not a claim about a specific real site
benchmarkContext.rule: Dry residue and accumulated soiling may remain visible. Generic wet sheen, active rain streak animation, or uniformly wet facade treatment is forbidden unless the environment context explicitly changes.

constructionReasoning.assembly: sliding aluminum sash and projecting sill/drip edge
constructionReasoning.mounting: frame fixed into facade opening; projecting sill/drip nose sheds rainfall outside the wall plane
interfaces: vertical runoff path on wall beneath drip points
constructionReasoning.orientationExposure: rain-exposed front facade with local recess shielding
constructionReasoning.agingCause: rain carries dust/mineral residue over discrete low points of the sill; gravity elongates marks downward; marks narrow/taper as water quantity falls
constructionReasoning.geometryVsMaterialDetail: sill projection and frame are geometry; runoff is a thin non-colliding decal-like mesh offset from the wall, never a box or painted highlight

constructionReasoning.assembly: balcony slab fascia and metal rail base fixing
constructionReasoning.mounting: rail posts mechanically anchored through base plates at the slab edge
constructionReasoning.orientationExposure: sun and rain exposed; strong drying between rainfall events
constructionReasoning.agingCause: water exits low points at the slab edge; isolated coating damage at ferrous fixtures can create localized iron-oxide runoff
constructionReasoning.geometryVsMaterialDetail: fasteners, base plates, slab lips remain physical geometry; only sparse residue is decal-like microgeometry

constructionReasoning.mounting: pipe is held off the wall by regularly spaced mechanical clamps
constructionReasoning.orientationExposure: concentrated rainwater path with repeated wetting near one facade line
constructionReasoning.agingCause: small leakage/splash and repeated wetting concentrate mineral/biological soiling close to the installed drainage path; effect falls off rapidly with distance
constructionReasoning.geometryVsMaterialDetail: pipe/clamps/bolts are geometry; wall residue is a tapered surface mesh following the installed path

constructionReasoning.mounting: not a mounted component; it is the physical interface between vertical wall and exterior grade
constructionReasoning.orientationExposure: maximum splash exposure occurs close to grade and increases near concentrated drainage
constructionReasoning.agingCause: soil-laden droplets and splashback deposit dirt with height-limited energy; staining must decay upward rather than form a uniform rectangle
constructionReasoning.geometryVsMaterialDetail: irregular band edge is explicit decal-like mesh geometry; no baked shadow, no primitive cube

constructionReasoning.mounting: flexible drain hose routes from the outdoor unit toward the balcony floor termination
constructionReasoning.orientationExposure: sheltered balcony floor; episodic condensate during AC use rather than rainfall
constructionReasoning.agingCause: repeated condensate can leave a small mineral/dust residue at the actual hose termination even when the dry benchmark is captured
constructionReasoning.geometryVsMaterialDetail: hose remains physical pipe geometry; only a small horizontal residue patch is decal-like mesh

materialDefinitions.baseColor_linearIntent: subtle neutral green-grey darkening; no black painted streak
materialDefinitions.specularF0: inherits dielectric substrate response; overlay must not introduce metallic reflection
materialDefinitions.microstructure: primarily deposited film/color and roughness change; thickness too small for modeled relief at benchmark distance
materialDefinitions.uvAging: persistent mineral/organic residue may fade slowly; no emissive or glossy response
materialDefinitions.angularFresnelResponse: must remain subordinate to underlying concrete/sash optics; no painted grazing highlight

materialDefinitions.microstructure: sub-mm particulate deposit represented by substrate microdetail rather than thick relief
materialDefinitions.uvAging: upper edge fades and erodes faster than protected low band
materialDefinitions.angularFresnelResponse: diffuse deposit; must not create a specular stripe

materialDefinitions.microstructure: oxide/mineral staining on concrete, not exposed bulk steel
materialDefinitions.uvAging: older stains desaturate and diffuse at edges
materialDefinitions.angularFresnelResponse: non-metallic because the visible mark is oxide residue on concrete

materialDefinitions.baseColor_linearIntent: very subtle neutral mineral/dust ring at hose termination
materialDefinitions.microstructure: thin deposit; no puddle geometry in dry benchmark
materialDefinitions.uvAging: sheltered; slower UV fade than exposed facade
materialDefinitions.angularFresnelResponse: no artificial wet highlight without active condensate evidence

distributionRules.windowRunoff: one narrow tapered path per physical sill; lateral position, length and drift vary deterministically but remain inside the sill catchment
distributionRules.balconyDrip: one or occasionally two short tapered marks per physical slab lip; never a repeated full-width stripe
distributionRules.railRust: sparse subset only (approximately 19 percent of physical rail base plates) to represent localized coating failure without procedural repetition
distributionRules.gradeSplash: continuous low band with height increased near the real downpipe side; hard-clamped to physically credible splash height
distributionRules.downpipeRunoff: concentrated at the installed downpipe line only
distributionRules.acResidue: small horizontal patch at each modeled drain-hose termination; dry residue only

lodPolicy.LOD0: all five weathering mesh groups available for 4K hero/oblique/grazing inspection
lodPolicy.LOD1: may retain grade and primary runoff while reducing sparse micro-streak density after render verification
lodPolicy.LOD2: only low-frequency grade/downpipe context if still perceptible
lodPolicy.LOD3: weathering may be omitted when below pixel contribution threshold
lodPolicy.currentImplementationNote: weathering detail is currently grouped into five combined meshes to reduce renderer cost; distance-specific LOD switching remains render/performance verification work

automaticFailConditions: stain with no physical source upstream or at interface
rust residue treated as metallic bulk metal
uniform wet facade in dry benchmark
obvious repeated stain spacing or identical streak silhouette
weathering geometry z-fighting/interpenetration visible in benchmark crop
weathering used to hide a light leak, geometry seam, or missing construction

checks: streak width and opacity remain subdominant at native 3840x2160
no z-fighting or transparent sorting rectangles
grade splash does not read as a painted horizontal band
rail rust remains sparse and source-anchored
weathering does not erase substrate PBR response
no repeated procedural pattern is immediately obvious at 100 percent crops
